decisions.summary: mechanism() reads a make word as a target only when it does not open with '-'; a flag is never read past, so in `make -C <tree> <target>` the target behind -C is never read, and that miss (a new target written behind a flag) is added to the function's MISSES list
decisions.why: The fix stops the refusal of correct work, as T431's line asks, but it does so by leaving the sizing check blind on `make -C <tree> <target>`. That is the form both of the block's own fixture lines (T369, T437) use, and the form this project's pool-tree commands take. So a brief whose line names a NEW target as `make -C <tree> new-thing` is now sized as one builder with nothing refusing. That is a check passing bad work, a defect by constitution XIV, on the sizing rule the GM asked the tooling to enforce (T334: the coordinating session broke builder-brief.md's sizing rules 'with nothing refusing'; 2026-11-19: 'make sure all of the enforcement is real enforcement and not just instructions'). None of the three grounds holds. Reading past a flag's argument is not impossible: only a short, documented set of make flags take one (-C, -f, -I, -o, -W and their long forms, with or without '='). The reason given ('would need make's flag grammar', 'the algorithmically easier route') is implementation cost, which is not a ground. The simpler-route rule picks between routes that both work, not a route that knowingly leaves a check passing bad work. The block also names the miss and then writes 'Found and left? none'. A known defect left unfixed goes in Found-and-left with its reason, a filed task and its order (FR-009, and the form T432's block uses for T479), not in a MISSES comment.
